learningObjective: Contrast fully shape-specialized compilation with dynamic-shape compilation and identify the trade-offs each incurs.
stem: Consider a compiler that must handle both fully shape-specialized compilation (one compiled artifact per shape combination) and dynamic-shape compilation (one artifact valid across a shape range). Which of the following statements are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Shape-specialized artifacts can apply optimizations that require known constants (e.g., loop-tripcount-dependent unrolling, tile sizes tuned to exact dimensions) that a dynamic-shape artifact cannot use for the same code path.

Dynamic-shape artifacts trade some per-shape performance for reduced compilation time and reduced storage of many specialized kernels; symbolic shapes let the compiler emit one kernel with runtime-dispatched tail handling.
Fully shape-specialized compilation is always faster at runtime because it avoids all runtime dispatch, even for shapes seen only once during serving.
Dynamic-shape compilation is semantically incorrect for models with shape-dependent numerics (e.g., a broadcast that depends on the runtime shape); shape specialization is required for correctness.
A hybrid strategy — bucket runtime shapes into a small number of buckets and specialize each — can capture much of the per-shape speed while bounding compile time and cache size.

explanation: A captures the fundamental optimization advantage of shape specialization. B captures the fundamental cost/storage/compile-time advantage of dynamic shapes; symbolic-shape emitters (TorchInductor with `dynamic=True`, TVM Relax with symbolic shapes) do exactly this. E is a well-known engineering compromise. C is false: for shapes seen once, specialization pays the compile-time cost that dominates the runtime saving. D is false: dynamic-shape compilation is semantics-preserving; the compiler symbolically tracks broadcast, and correctness does not depend on shape being a compile-time constant.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: canonical advantage of shape specialization.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: canonical advantage of dynamic shape.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: single-use shapes make specialization a compile-time loss.
optionExplanations.E: Correct: bucket-and-specialize is a common production strategy.

assumptions: The compiler supports both modes and can bucket if desired.
nonImplications: Does not imply dynamic-shape compilation is universally worse at runtime; on some backends symbolic tiling reaches within 5-10% of specialized.
Does not imply bucketing is free — extra buckets add compile time and code size.

distractorRationales.C: Ignores compile-time amortization for single-use shapes.
